blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the rise level, transport, storage, handling and distribution stop being four separate activities and become one continuous flow that must be balanced against each other. More storage means less urgent transport. Faster handling means less storage. Smart distribution means fewer emergency trips. Each choice affects the others.

The manager's job is to adjust the balance as conditions change. When demand spikes, handling and distribution must be speeded up, and storage temporarily tolerated. When demand drops, storage becomes painful and transport can be consolidated to save cost.

What separates a good logistics manager from an average one is the willingness to make small, deliberate adjustments every week — rather than waiting for a crisis to force big, expensive ones.

items.q: According to the text, how should transport, storage, handling and distribution be treated at the rise level?
options: As tasks handled by different managers
As one continuous flow balanced against each other
As stages that never affect one another
items.why: "become one continuous flow that must be balanced against each other" — deixam de ser quatro atividades separadas.

items.q: According to the text, what happens to transport when demand drops?
options: It can be consolidated to save cost
items.why: "When demand drops… transport can be consolidated to save cost."

items.q: The text suggests that a good logistics manager is mainly distinguished by…
options: waiting for a crisis before acting
avoiding any change until data is complete
keeping storage as high as possible
items.why: "the willingness to make small, deliberate adjustments every week — rather than waiting for a crisis."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: It is safer to leave the balance untouched until a crisis forces a change.
The four activities should be managed as one system.
A decision about storage can change how much transport is needed.
Regular small adjustments are cheaper than late big ones.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende ajustes pequenos e frequentes justamente para evitar a mudança grande e cara na crise.

items.q: The line "More storage means less urgent transport" suggests that…
options: gaining in one activity relieves pressure on another
items.why: Inferência: as atividades são trade-offs — reforçar uma alivia a pressão sobre a outra.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily orientando o novo gerente de área. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, every Friday I sit down for about an hour and look at three numbers together: how full the warehouse is, how many people we have on handling, and what's booked on transport for the coming week. I never look at them separately — that's the mistake most people make.

Let me show you this week. Demand from the north sites is climbing, so handling has to be speeded up and I've pulled two extra people onto the floor. That means the trucks can leave fuller and later, and we avoid three emergency runs that would have cost us a fortune.

Down south it's the opposite. Orders have dropped, the shelves are packed, and storage is starting to hurt. So I've consolidated four small deliveries into one route on Wednesday. Slower for the customer by half a day, but far cheaper for us.

The whole point is that I make tiny moves every week. If you wait, the pressure builds until you're forced into a big, panicked decision that costs ten times more. And write down what you change — the next person needs to understand why.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How often does Emily review the three numbers together?
items.why: "every Friday I sit down for about an hour and look at three numbers together."

items.q: Which three things does Emily look at together?
options: Storage cost, insurance and delivery times
Fuel prices, driver hours and customer complaints
How full the warehouse is, handling staff, and booked transport
items.why: "how full the warehouse is, how many people we have on handling, and what's booked on transport."

items.q: Why did Emily add two extra people to handling at the north sites?
options: Because demand was climbing and handling had to be speeded up
items.why: "Demand from the north sites is climbing, so handling has to be speeded up and I've pulled two extra people onto the floor."

items.q: What can we infer about Emily's decision in the south?
options: She refuses to change anything until orders recover
She always prioritises speed over cost
She accepts a slightly slower delivery to cut cost when storage is painful
items.why: Inferência: ela consolida quatro entregas em uma, aceitando meio dia a mais para reduzir custo — trade-off consciente.

items.q: What is Emily's main message to the new manager?
options: Big decisions are always better than small ones
Storage should never be allowed to rise
The customer should always come first
Small weekly moves prevent forced, costly ones later
items.why: Inferência: "I make tiny moves every week. If you wait, the pressure builds until you're forced into a big, panicked decision."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We treat the four activities as one continuous flow." A continuous flow is…
items.why: Continuous flow = fluxo contínuo: um movimento ininterrupto e conectado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When demand suddenly ___, handling has to be speeded up."
items.why: To spike = disparar: subir de forma brusca e repentina.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Four small deliveries were ___ into one route to cut cost."
items.why: To consolidate = consolidar: juntar várias em uma só.

items.q: "These were small but deliberate changes." Deliberate means…
options: done on purpose and with intention
items.why: Deliberate = deliberado: feito de propósito, com intenção.

items.q: "High storage was tolerated for a week until demand settled." Tolerated here means…
options: accepted for the time being, though not ideal
items.why: Tolerated = tolerado: aceito temporariamente, mesmo sem ser o ideal.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de logística e operações. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The area manager still has to sign off on the weekly plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new routing model site by site." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two drivers pushed back on the tighter schedule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to consolidate the routes but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A few extra trucks won't move the needle on our storage cost." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
